title: Mock 5 · Exit & Estate
blurb: NPS exit slabs and drawdown, corpus adjustments, distribution products, gifts, nominations and RA compliance.

questions.q: Which product feature directly addresses longevity risk, the risk of outliving one's retirement savings?
options: A credit card with a high limit
A deferred annuity bought at 65 that pays income for life from age 85
questions.explanation: The workbook gives the example of a deferred annuity purchased at 65 that pays income from 85 for life as a way to take care of longevity risk.
hints: Wrong: borrowing is not a retirement income source.
Correct: lifetime income starting late hedges longevity.
Wrong: a debt fund can run out and offers no lifetime guarantee.
Wrong: a 5-year FD ends long before late old age.

questions.q: Ravi needs ₹50,000 four years from now. If money can earn 7% a year compounded annually, how much should he set aside today?
hints: Wrong: this deducts simple interest of 7% × 4 from 50,000.
Wrong: this discounts for only one year.
Wrong: this compounds forward instead of discounting.

questions.q: Which bond would show the greatest fall in price if market interest rates rise sharply?
options: A floating-rate bond that resets quarterly
The bond with the shortest residual maturity
The bond with the highest duration
The bond with the highest credit rating
questions.explanation: Interest rate risk depends on duration: the higher the duration, the greater the sensitivity of price to rate changes.
hints: Wrong: floating-rate coupons reset with the market, so rate risk is low.
Wrong: short maturity means low duration and low sensitivity.
Correct: higher duration means larger price changes.
Wrong: credit rating affects default risk, not rate sensitivity.

questions.q: What is the current status of the Mahila Samman Savings Certificate, according to the workbook?
options: Closed to new deposits since 1 April 2025; existing accounts run to their 2-year maturity
Open only to senior women citizens
Open to all women with a ₹30 lakh limit
questions.explanation: The enrolment window expired on 31 March 2025; no fresh deposits have been accepted since 1 April 2025, while existing accounts continue to maturity.
hints: Correct: closed for new deposits, existing accounts continue.
Wrong: no such conversion took place.
Wrong: the scheme was open to women and girls of any age, and is now closed.
Wrong: the scheme is closed and its limit was ₹2 lakh.

questions.q: Corporate bonds in India are typically issued for tenors ranging from:
options: 2 years to 15 years, with 5- and 7-year tenors popular
questions.explanation: Corporate bonds are issued for tenors ranging from two years to 15 years; 5-year and 7-year bonds are the more popular tenors.
hints: Wrong: very long tenors are typical of government securities.
Wrong: this describes money market instruments.
Correct: 2-15 years, 5 and 7 popular.
Wrong: corporate bonds normally have fixed maturities.

questions.q: When a client already holds investments earmarked for retirement, how does the adviser adjust the monthly savings required?
options: Deduct their current value from the corpus needed
Deduct the future value of those investments at retirement from the corpus needed, then compute savings on the gap
Ignore them, since they may be used elsewhere
Add them to the corpus required
questions.explanation: The steps are: select investments, estimate their return, calculate their future value at retirement, deduct it from the corpus required, and calculate periodic savings on the balance.
hints: Wrong: current value ignores the growth until retirement.
Correct: use future value, then PMT on the gap.
Wrong: suitable existing assets should be assigned to the goal.
Wrong: existing assets reduce, not increase, the requirement.

questions.q: Sunil earns ₹12 lakh a year, expects income to grow 8% a year, retires in 20 years and assumes a 70% income replacement ratio. Approximately what annual income will he need at retirement?
questions.explanation: Income at retirement = 12,00,000 × 1.08^20 ≈ ₹55.93 lakh; × 70% ≈ ₹39.15 lakh.
hints: Correct: 55.93 lakh × 0.70.
Wrong: this uses simple growth before applying 70%.
Wrong: this is the projected income before applying the ratio.
Wrong: this applies 70% to today's income without growth.

questions.q: Two retirees earn the same average return over 5 years, but one suffers losses in the first two years while both withdraw the same amount each year. The one with early losses ends with less money. This illustrates:
questions.explanation: In a portfolio making regular withdrawals, bad returns early in retirement cause permanent damage because more units must be sold at depressed prices. This is sequence-of-returns risk.
hints: Wrong: no currency exposure is involved.
Wrong: reinvestment risk concerns reinvesting coupons at lower rates.
Correct: the order of returns matters when withdrawing.
Wrong: credit risk concerns issuer default.

questions.q: An investor buys a stock because it has risen sharply over the past few weeks, expecting the rise to continue. Which bias is this?
questions.explanation: Recency bias is extrapolating recent events into the future and expecting them to repeat.
hints: Wrong: anchoring sticks to an old reference point.
Wrong: inaction from fear of loss is the opposite behaviour.
Wrong: familiarity bias is choosing known or comfortable assets.
Correct: recent performance is being projected forward.

questions.q: A subscriber who joins NPS after the age of 65 chooses the Auto option. What is the maximum equity exposure allowed?
questions.explanation: If the subscriber joins beyond 65, the maximum equity exposure is 15% under Auto choice and 50% under Active choice.
hints: Correct: 15% under Auto.
Wrong: not the limit given for joiners after 65.
Wrong: 50% is the Active choice cap for such subscribers.
Wrong: 75% is the general Active choice cap.

questions.q: An All Citizen subscriber reaches 60 with an NPS corpus of ₹11 lakh. Which option is available besides the standard 80:20 route?
options: Withdraw up to ₹6 lakh as lump sum; use the balance for an annuity or SUR for at least 6 years
Withdraw the entire ₹11 lakh as lump sum
Withdraw up to ₹2 lakh; annuitise the rest
questions.explanation: Where the corpus is more than ₹8 lakh and up to ₹12 lakh, the subscriber may withdraw up to ₹6 lakh as lump sum and use the balance for annuity or SUR for at least six years, or follow 80:20.
hints: Wrong: 60:40 is the Government sector ratio.
Correct: the ₹8-12 lakh slab allows ₹6 lakh lump sum.
Wrong: full withdrawal is allowed only up to ₹8 lakh for a normal exit (₹12 lakh only if joined after 60).
Wrong: ₹2 lakh is the NPS-Lite/Swavalamban threshold.

questions.q: An NPS account is frozen because the minimum contribution was not made in a year. What must the subscriber do to unfreeze it?
options: Pay a penalty of ₹100 per year of default
Transfer funds from Tier II to Tier I
questions.explanation: To unfreeze the account, the subscriber is required to make a minimum contribution of ₹500.
hints: Correct: ₹500 unfreezes the account.
Wrong: a person can hold only one NPS account.
Wrong: no such penalty is specified in the workbook.
Wrong: if Tier I is frozen, Tier II is frozen too.

questions.q: Under the NPS drawdown Systematic Payout Rate (SPR) method, what is the SPR for a subscriber aged 60 who chooses a Drawdown End Age of 85?
questions.explanation: SPR = 1 ÷ (Drawdown End Age − Current Age) = 1 ÷ (85 − 60) = 4.00%.
hints: Wrong: this does not follow the SPR formula.
Wrong: this would be 1/60, using age instead of the remaining years.
Correct: 1/25 = 4%.
Wrong: this would be 1/40.

questions.q: How many nominees can an NPS subscriber register for a Tier I account?
options: Up to 3, with the percentage share specified
questions.explanation: A subscriber can make a maximum of three nominations to the Tier I account and specify the percentage allocated to each; the total must add up to 100%.
hints: Correct: up to three nominees.
Wrong: the number is capped and shares are specified.
Wrong: the maximum is three.
Wrong: more than one nominee is allowed.

questions.q: When comparing a fund's performance with peer funds, what caution does the workbook emphasise?
options: Only compare absolute returns over one month
Always prefer the fund with the largest AUM
Consider the risk taken, since a fund may outperform peers by taking much higher risk
questions.explanation: In comparing peer funds it is good to consider both return and risk; a fund may outperform peers but may have taken significantly higher risks.
hints: Wrong: short absolute comparisons are not the workbook's approach.
Wrong: differences in management must be kept in mind.
Wrong: size is not a measure of performance.
Correct: returns must be judged alongside risk.

questions.q: Among comparable schemes, which one should an investor ideally prefer on a risk-adjusted basis?
options: The scheme with the highest standard deviation
The scheme with the lowest NAV
The scheme with the highest Sharpe ratio
The scheme with the highest beta
questions.explanation: Investors ought to prefer the scheme with the highest Sharpe ratio, since it generates a higher return for each unit of risk taken.
hints: Wrong: higher SD means more volatility.
Wrong: NAV level says nothing about performance.
Correct: highest return per unit of risk.
Wrong: higher beta means more market risk.

questions.q: Kisan Vikas Patra (at 7.7% interest) doubles the amount invested in:
questions.explanation: The workbook states the amount invested in KVP doubles in 124 months, calculated at 7.7% interest.
hints: Wrong: not the KVP doubling period.
Correct: 124 months.
Wrong: not the KVP doubling period.
Wrong: not the KVP doubling period.

questions.q: For a married couple applying jointly for a reverse mortgage loan, what are the age conditions?
options: One spouse must be above 60 and the other not below 55
At least one spouse must be above 55
questions.explanation: For joint borrowers, at least one must be above 60 years and the other not below 55 years.
hints: Correct: 60 and 55.
Wrong: the primary borrower must be above 60.
Wrong: not the condition in the workbook.
Wrong: the second spouse can be 55 or more.

questions.q: In the bucket strategy, what equity exposure does the workbook suggest for the second (safety-cushion) bucket?
options: At least 50% in mid and small caps
Lower-risk equity not exceeding 20% of the portfolio
100% equity, since it is not needed for 20 years
questions.explanation: The second bucket can hold long-term income funds, FMPs, bonds, real estate, gold and lower-risk equity not exceeding 20% of the portfolio.
hints: Wrong: bucket 2 is not meant for aggressive equity.
Wrong: some equity is allowed in bucket 2.
Correct: up to 20% lower-risk equity.
Wrong: that describes neither bucket 2 nor its horizon.

questions.q: In constructing diversified retirement income, the workbook suggests investments in bonds and debentures be used mainly for:
options: Accumulating funds for medium-term goals such as travel in retirement
Providing the growth element of the portfolio
Meeting mandatory expenses such as taxes and insurance
questions.explanation: Investments in bonds and debentures can be used to accumulate funds for medium-term goals such as travel in retirement.
hints: Correct: medium-term goals.
Wrong: mutual funds bring growth.
Wrong: emergency funds sit in bucket 1's liquid assets.
Wrong: guaranteed pension and annuity are earmarked for mandatory expenses.

questions.q: For tax purposes, what standard deduction is allowed on the net annual value of rental income, after deducting municipal taxes?
questions.explanation: Rental income is adjusted for municipal taxes paid; from this net annual value a standard deduction of 30% is allowed, plus interest on a loan taken to buy the property.
hints: Wrong: not the rate in the workbook.
Wrong: not the rate in the workbook.
Wrong: not the rate in the workbook.
Correct: 30% standard deduction.

questions.q: Which of the following gifts received by an individual is exempt from tax as per the workbook?
options: A gift from a business associate
A gift received on the occasion of marriage
A gift from a friend of any amount
Cash received from an unrelated person
questions.explanation: Gifts from specified relatives, any gift received on the occasion of marriage and gifts inherited under a will are exempt from tax.
hints: Wrong: business associates are not specified relatives.
Correct: marriage gifts are exempt.
Wrong: friends are not specified relatives.
Wrong: unrelated persons are not covered by the exemption.

questions.q: If there is a legal dispute among heirs after the death of the first holder of a jointly held asset, the joint holder's right to operate the asset:
options: Is absolute and cannot be questioned
Can be superseded by the will or succession law
questions.explanation: In the event of the death of the first holder, access passes to the joint holder; but if there is a legal contest, the joint holder's operational right can be superseded by succession law or the will.
hints: Wrong: operational access is not ownership.
Wrong: there is no such conversion.
Wrong: the bank does not take ownership.
Correct: the will or succession law prevails.

questions.q: How many trustees must the Board of the NPS Trust have?
options: A minimum of 7 and a maximum of 15
A minimum of 5 and a maximum of 11
questions.explanation: The Board of Trustees shall have a minimum of five and a maximum of eleven trustees.
hints: Wrong: the range is 5 to 11.
Wrong: the minimum is five.
Wrong: it is a range, not a fixed number.
Correct: 5 to 11 trustees.

questions.q: A non-individual Retirement Adviser changes its compliance officer. Within what period must PFRDA be informed?
questions.explanation: Any change in the compliance officer should be intimated to the Authority within seven days.
hints: Wrong: 3 days is the grievance acknowledgement period.
Wrong: 30 days is the grievance resolution period.
Wrong: 90 days is the Ombudsman's award deadline.
Correct: within 7 days.
